title: Dense linear orders: rational embeddings and the real line
summary: Countable orders embed in the rationals, while density and completeness characterize the rational and real orders.
abstract: Between any two rational numbers there is another, yet rational numbers leave gaps that the real numbers fill. Every countable linear order can be represented by a subset of the rationals with its usual order. If a countable order also has a point between every two points and has no first or last point, it has exactly the order structure of the rationals. Filling all its gaps produces the real order: every nonempty complete dense order without endpoints and with a countable dense subset has exactly the order structure of the real line.

based_on.title: An Introduction to Set Theory
based_on.pages: 79–82 (Chapter 8, Theorem 29 and the complete separable order characterization)
